one_line_premise: In the winter of 1636–37 a flower briefly cost a fortune, then nothing; the legend that followed grew bigger than the crash.
central_question: How did a tulip bulb become worth a fortune, and did its collapse really ruin the Dutch?

sources.title: Tulipmania: Money, Honor, and Knowledge in the Dutch Golden Age
Memoirs of Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds

people.name: Carolus Clusius
people.role_in_story: Botanist who planted tulips in Leiden's Hortus Botanicus in 1593

people.name: Charles Mackay
people.role_in_story: Scottish journalist whose 1841 book popularised the tulip mania story

people.name: Anne Goldgar
people.role_in_story: Historian, author of Tulipmania (2007), an archival study of the trade

timeline.title: Clusius plants tulips in Leiden
timeline.what_happened: Carolus Clusius plants his tulip collection in the new Hortus Botanicus of Leiden.

timeline.title: Speculators enter the tulip market
timeline.what_happened: Partly driven by French demand, speculators begin to trade bulb contracts.

timeline.title: Even common bulbs rise
timeline.what_happened: Contracts change hands in tavern 'colleges', some five times; even common bulbs rise in price.

timeline.title: The Haarlem auction without buyers
timeline.what_happened: According to a contemporary satire, an auctioneer in Haarlem finds no buyers despite lowering his price several times.

timeline.title: Last day of the bubble
timeline.what_happened: 98 sales are recorded at wildly varying prices; by the end of the first week of February prices have collapsed.

timeline.title: The florists' guild converts contracts
timeline.what_happened: The guild of Dutch florists turns contracts written after 30 November 1636 into options buyers can cancel for a fee.

timeline.title: Mackay publishes his account
timeline.what_happened: Charles Mackay's Extraordinary Popular Delusions popularises the tulip mania story.

timeline.title: Goldgar publishes Tulipmania
timeline.what_happened: Anne Goldgar's archival study challenges the traditional account.
